title: Frontend: Username/password admin sign-in for seeded credentials

requirements.summary: Add a username/password admin sign-in path (English-only UI text) that can authenticate with the seeded credentials and results in Admin-gated UI access.
acceptanceCriteria: The Login page provides a username/password sign-in path that works with username "Rushikesh" and password "123".
After successful login as the seeded Admin, the UI reflects Admin permissions (e.g., Admin route access is granted).
All login page labels, helper text, and error messages are in English.

file_operations.description: Update the login screen to include a username/password sign-in form for administrators (in addition to or instead of the current Internet Identity button), with all labels/helper text/errors in English. On submit, call the existing username/password authentication flow (via a backend capability exposed on the actor), persist any returned admin/session secret in sessionStorage (e.g., using existing URL/session utilities), then complete the sign-in flow so Admin permissions are reflected in the UI (Admin nav item visible and /admin accessible). Use the authorization component’s guidance for handling auth/authorization errors gracefully in UI; verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

Create a small auth helper hook for username/password sign-in that invokes the backend capability through the existing actor, manages loading/error state, and stores any required secret/session value for subsequent authorized calls. Keep error messages user-friendly and in English. Use the authorization component’s guidance for auth state handling (e.g., clearing cached data on logout); verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

Update the TypeScript backend interface typings to include the existing username/password authentication capability used by the login form (and any returned token/secret type), and align the UserProfile type with what the frontend expects (e.g., include role if returned by getCallerUserProfile) so Admin role checks are type-safe.

Ensure the auth context correctly derives Admin status after a successful username/password sign-in (e.g., by relying on role returned from getCallerUserProfile and/or admin-check capability) and that login-related state/messages remain English-only. Use the authorization component’s RBAC conventions for determining and reflecting Admin permissions; verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.
